learningObjective: Explain the standard GPU strategy for computing top-k over a large vocabulary and why full sort is not required.
stem: An LLM sampler needs to compute the top-k tokens per batch row over a [B, V] logits tensor, where V is typically 32K-200K and k is small (e.g. 50). Which GPU strategy is most appropriate?

options.text: Sort each row in full with a merge sort or radix sort of complexity O(V log V), then take the top k. This is essentially the only correct approach because partial-selection algorithms cannot guarantee stable order among ties.

Use a two-stage approach: partition each row into blocks, keep a per-block top-k with a small in-register heap or bitonic-select, then merge the per-block candidates into a single top-k with a final reduction. Total work is O(V log k), well below full-sort.
Compute softmax over the entire row and then threshold at 1 / (k * V); this yields top-k without any sort because the probability of the k-th largest logit is bounded above by 1/k in expectation.
Top-k is inherently sequential across the V dimension because each selection depends on all previous ones; the only GPU-friendly path is to move top-k to the CPU on a small logits copy over PCIe.

explanation: The standard GPU top-k algorithm partitions the row and keeps a small per-partition candidate set (top-k or top-K' with K' >= k) using a small heap/bitonic selection network in registers/SMEM; a final reduction merges these candidate sets into the global top-k. Total work per row is O(V log k) instead of O(V log V). No full sort is needed. Frameworks like cuDNN, cutlass, and inference engines (TRT-LLM, vLLM) use this pattern. Sampling then usually applies temperature/top-p on the resulting top-k set.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: the two-stage partitioned top-k is the canonical GPU approach.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: full sort is unnecessary and wasteful; log(V/k) work per element is enough.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: fabricates a mathematical relation; softmax thresholds do not give top-k.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: top-k is highly parallel; the partition+merge pattern is the standard.

assumptions: V is much larger than k so partitioning is beneficial.
Ties can be resolved with an arbitrary stable rule (e.g., lower index wins).
nonImplications: Does not imply that a fully sorted output is available; only the top-k values and indices.
Does not imply this is the only correct approach; approximate top-k, radix-based top-k, and heap-based top-k all exist.

sourceRefs.locator: Sort and selection primitives on GPU
